correctness.rationale: Under the exactly known continuous null the m=n+1 spacings have uniform Dirichlet law. The Pascal convolution represents every recursion level exactly and has bounded normalizers. Ordered-coordinate sectors have Jacobian D_max^m times products of adjacent scale ratios; the count H(S) of contained consecutive intervals gives the exact moment exponent 2/m, with equality only at two endpoint corners. Splitting radial Beta(m-1,1) mass from angular Dirichlet(1^(m-1)) yields R=K log(1/epsilon)-log Q(U)+O(epsilon) uniformly and, through dominated convergence plus stronger moments off the corners, the positive finite prefactor 2 E Q(U)^(-2/m). Checked 4912 finite assertions plus independent restricted-corner quadrature; numerical checks are corroboration, not infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: The central new claim is the exact fixed-n>=2 extreme-tail *coefficient* for the published RPS statistic and its endpoint-cluster interpretation, not the known n=1 CDF, the recursion itself, or generic singular-integral exponents. Main primary Sections 2-3 were read; the most relevant broader hyperplane-arrangement theorem and a later RPS application were inspected. No checked source stated or implied the displayed numerical/Dirichlet coefficient without a new calculation. Residual historical priority risk is explicit.
residual_risks: The 2023 doctoral thesis On non-parametric tests for discovery and limit setting in one and multiple dimensions is cited in the 2023 Physical Review D bibliography but its full text was not obtained; no claim that it fails to cover the result is made.

value.rationale: The original RPS paper uses simulated smooth CDF calibration for n>=2, including small quantiles around 1e-7. A sharp analytic far-tail law with an exact coefficient and a two-corner concentration mechanism is a motivated calibration benchmark; it identifies rare-event configurations and a nontrivial moment boundary that are not extractable from routine finite Monte Carlo. It is self-contained for each fixed n and does not overclaim usable finite-threshold accuracy.
